content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In mainstream Christian teaching, feet most commonly symbolize a person's 'walk'—that is, one's conduct, moral direction, and course of life. To have one's feet on a right path, kept from stumbling, or set upon a rock is read as living faithfully and obediently before God, while straying or slipping feet represent sin and moral failure.","primary_basis":["Psalm 119:105 ('a lamp to my feet and a light to my path')","Psalm 1:1 (the way/walk of the righteous vs. the wicked)","Proverbs 4:26-27 ('ponder the path of your feet')","Psalm 40:2 ('set my feet upon a rock')","Psalm 121:3 ('he will not let your foot be moved')","Proverbs 6:18 ('feet that make haste to run to evil')","Ephesians 6:15 (feet shod with readiness of the gospel of peace)","Luke 1:79 ('to guide our feet into the way of peace')"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Feet as the emblem of the messenger who proclaims good news—the 'beautiful feet' of gospel heralds and evangelists.","basis":["Isaiah 52:7","Nahum 1:15","Romans 10:15","Ephesians 6:15"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Feet as a symbol of dominion, victory, and subjection—enemies placed 'under the feet' of God, Christ, or his people.","basis":["Psalm 110:1","Psalm 8:6","1 Corinthians 15:25-27","Hebrews 2:8","Romans 16:20","Joshua 10:24","Genesis 3:15 (crushing the serpent's head, often linked)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Feet (especially footwashing) as a symbol of humility, servanthood, and cleansing from daily defilement—Christ washing the disciples' feet as the model of humble service and ongoing sanctification.","basis":["John 13:1-17","Luke 7:36-50 (the woman washing Jesus' feet)","1 Timothy 5:10","Genesis 18:4 and hospitality texts"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Sitting or falling at someone's feet as a posture of discipleship, worship, and submission to a teacher or to Christ.","basis":["Luke 10:39 (Mary at Jesus' feet)","Acts 22:3 (Paul 'at the feet of Gamaliel')","Revelation 1:17","Matthew 28:9"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The foot treading on land as a sign of taking possession or claiming inheritance/territory.","basis":["Joshua 1:3","Deuteronomy 11:24","Genesis 13:17 (walking the land)"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Feet in visionary imagery as a symbol of judgment, stability, or divine character—e.g., Christ's feet like burnished bronze, the iron-and-clay feet of Nebuchadnezzar's statue as fragile kingdoms, treading the winepress of wrath.","basis":["Revelation 1:15","Daniel 2:33-43","Revelation 19:15","Isaiah 63:3"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Feet as the humble but necessary members of the body of Christ, teaching mutual dependence within the church.","basis":["1 Corinthians 12:15, 12:21"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"medium","notes":"Feet do not carry one single settled symbolic meaning in Christian interpretation; the meaning is strongly context-dependent. The 'walk of life' sense is arguably the broadest and most frequently invoked in devotional and homiletical use, but the messenger motif (Isa 52:7/Rom 10:15), dominion motif (Ps 110:1), and humility/footwashing motif (John 13) are each robust, well-attested strands with their own liturgical and doctrinal traditions (e.g., Maundy Thursday footwashing; christological use of Ps 110). Any claim that feet have one fixed symbolic meaning across Scripture would exceed the recognizable consensus, which treats the symbol as a cluster of related but distinct usages."}
